Cost modeling (high-level rationale):
- Workload profile: short chat-like requests (avg 300 tokens total), heavy request fanout during campaigns (peak concurrency multiple). Baseline sustained qps estimate = 1,200 rps; peak burst up to 10k rps for minutes.
- Proposed reserved commit strategy: monthly committed baseline for steady throughput + small burst pool on demand. Recommend initial commit = capacity equivalent of 12 GPUs (24/7) to cover baseline 70% of traffic; keep 4 GPU hot spare pool for headroom; burst to cloud on short spikes.
- Unit economics examples (modeled):
  * Committed config cost: $58,000 / month for 12 reserved GPUs (example Redwood pricing illustrative).
  * Expected sustained utilization: 65-75% during business hours -> effective token cost = ~$0.00055/token (modeling avg 300 tokens/request at 1,200 rps baseline).
  * If utilization falls to 40% (non-peak), unit cost jumps to ~$0.0010/token.
  * On-demand-only (no commit) runs ~2x bill vs committed for steady workloads due to premium and lower packing efficiency.
- Sensitivity: small reductions in commit (12 -> 8 GPUs) reduce monthly commit cost but push more requests to on-demand bursts; breakeven point estimated when average utilization <50%.

SLA & negotiation points Helix cares about:
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile targets by token-length bucket (e.g., <=120ms @512 tokens; <=250ms @4k tokens). Want clear measurement method and dashboards.
- Throughput guarantee: committed baseline + documented burst handling policy (how requests are routed when baseline saturated).
- Credits: financial SLA credits tied to monthly %downtime and tail latency misses for specific routes. Helix insists on credit cap and faster incident response SLA.
- Security: KMS integration, tenant-level audit trail, SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning. Data residency: logs retained in NA for at least 3 years; option to restrict model cache persistence.
- Exit & scale clauses: 90-day right to terminate for material misses; 6-month step-up to increase commit with pre-agreed pricing bands.
